requires_concepts: local energy bounds with retained excitations

outputs.exact_statement:
In the same iterated limit, uniformly over all ground states, $$1-B_{N,L,a}(\Gamma)
   =\frac8{3\sqrt\pi}\sqrt{\rho a^3}+o(\sqrt{\rho a^3}).$$

For every nonempty allowed configuration set with nontrivial form domain, the full labelled and bosonic Dirichlet operators have compact resolvent and the same lowest energy. A bosonic ground vector is therefore also a ground vector of the full labelled operator. Its modulus is a nonnegative bosonic ground vector. A form-domain function restricts, for almost every choice of some fixed coordinates, to the Dirichlet form domain of the open allowed set in the remaining coordinates. Zero extension of such a slice remains admissible if obstacles contributed by the fixed coordinates are removed.

For all sufficiently large $D$, uniformly in [set:scales], $$\label{set:removal-bound} E_N-E_{N-m}\le C\alpha m\qquad(0\le m\le N).$$ At fixed $K,r$, the ratio $E_n/n$ is nondecreasing among positive particle numbers having nonempty form domain.

For $A\subset\mathcal L$ set $$f_A(X)=\sum_{i=1}^N e^{-d_K(x_i,A)},
 \qquad f_{\varnothing}=0,$$ where the distance is to the set of site centers. Every normalized nonnegative bosonic ground function obeys $$\label{set:count-mgf-bound}
 \log\int e^{z f_A}\,\mathrm d\mu\le CzD|A|
               \qquad(0\le z\le1).$$ The constants are uniform for $K\ge100$, $D$ sufficiently large, and $\alpha\in I_\alpha$.

There are constants $c,C>0$ and an exponent $c_{\mathrm r}>0$, independent of the sufficiently small box exponent $\theta$, such that, for $0\le n\le6Dv_b$, $$\label{en:rough-ineq} \begin{split} H_n\ge {}&\frac{4\pi r n^2}{v_b}-Cv_bD^{1-c_{\mathrm r}} +c\,\mathrm d\Gamma\bigl(\min\{p^2,1\}\bigr)\\ &\quad+cD\sum_A |A|\, \mathfrak h\left(\frac{n_A}{D|A|}-\frac{n}{Dv_b}\right), \qquad \mathfrak h(t)=\frac{t^2}{1+|t|}. \end{split}$$ Here $p$ denotes the Neumann frequency and $\mathrm d\Gamma$ sums the indicated one-particle operator over all particles. One may take $c_{\mathrm r}=10^{-3}$.
Let $\psi$ belong to the form domain of $H_n$, and let $V_n=\sum_{i

For $n$ in [en:middle-sector] and a bosonic $n$-particle vector $\psi$ in the form domain of $H_b$ satisfying $\psi=\mathbf 1_{\{n_L\le M/4\}}\psi$, $$\label{en:sharp-bound} \langle\psi,H_b\psi\rangle \ge\{v_be_r(n/v_b)-Cv_bQ^{-1/4}\}\|\psi\|^2 +cE^{-2}\langle n_++K_Hn_H\rangle_\psi +c\mathcal B(\psi).$$ The constants are uniform in the particle sector and in spectator variables.

Let $n$ satisfy [en:middle-sector], $|z|^2\le2n$, and $\xi=\mathbf 1_{\{n_+\le n,\ n_L\le M/4\}}\xi$. For every fixed $\delta>0$ and sufficiently large $D$, $$\begin{aligned} \langle\xi,\mathcal H_0(z)\xi\rangle &\ge 4\pi c_{\rm L}(a')^{5/2}v_b\rho_z^{5/2}\|\xi\|^2 +\sum_{p\ne0}\widetilde D_p(z)\|b_p(z)\xi\|^2 -\delta\langle S\rangle_\xi -C_\delta v_bQ^{-1/4}\|\xi\|^2 . \label{en:small-gap-bound} \end{aligned}$$

Let $n$ satisfy [en:middle-sector], let $|z|^2\le2n$, and restrict the excitation space to $n_+\le n$ and $n_L\le M/4$. On this space the exact cosine expansion may replace the coefficients in (2.35)–(2.37) of [[FJGMOT](#ref-FJGMOT)]. Its correction is bounded in absolute quadratic form by $$\delta\left(S+\sum_{p\ne0}\widetilde D_p(z)b_p(z)^*b_p(z)\right) +C_\delta v_bQ^{-1/4}$$ for every fixed $\delta>0$, if $D$ is sufficiently large.

For $E\asymp Q=D^\theta$, $\theta=u$ or $w$, the following quantities have sum at most $CVQ^{-1/5}$:* 1. *the box-count penalty $$\sum_b Dv_b\,\mathfrak h\left(\frac{n_b}{Dv_b}-1\right) \quad\text{in expectation};$$* 2. *on middle-sector high pieces, the expectations of $$\sum_{p\ne0}\min(p^2,1)a_p^*a_p +D\sum_{A\in\mathcal C_d,\ A\subset b} |A|\mathfrak h(q_A-1);$$* 3. *on low pieces, the expectations of $E^{-2}(n_++K_Hn_H)$ and the quantities $\mathcal B(\psi)$;* 4. *on sectors outside [en:middle-sector], their total $(n_b+Dv_b)$-weighted squared norms.* *The first quantity is evaluated on the original vector. The other quantities are evaluated on the indicated localized restrictions.

On the $n$-particle space, for every vector $\xi$, $$\label{en:fourth-block-bound}
 \|X^2\xi\|^2\le Cn^2\langle\xi,(n_++2)^2\xi\rangle.$$

Use the nested partitions and limiting convention of Section 2, with the exponents chosen above. Let $A=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal C_B}A_b$, where the one-particle operators $A_b$ on $L^2(b)$ are identical in local coordinates and satisfy $0\le A_b\le W$. Their cosine matrices may be complex Hermitian. For every normalized bosonic ground vector, $$\label{mom:local-covariance-formula} \frac1V\langle\mathrm d\Gamma(A)\rangle =\frac1{v_b}\sum_{p\ne0}(A_b)_{pp}F_\alpha(p)+o(1), \qquad (A_b)_{pp}=\langle u_p,A_bu_p\rangle.$$ The error is uniform in the ground vector and in all the indicated operators, which may depend on the scales. The same formula and uniformity hold when $A_b=WC_bW$ and $C_b$ is any complex contraction, identical in local coordinates. Both assertions hold uniformly for simultaneous translates of the nested partitions.

Let $E=B$, $n$ satisfy [en:middle-sector], and $|z|^2\le2n$. For $0\le A_b\le W$ and an excitation vector $\xi$ in the form domain of $n_+$, put $$\mathcal Q_z(\xi)=\sum_{p\ne0}\widetilde D_p(z)\|b_p(z)\xi\|^2, \qquad T_A(z)=\sum_{p\ne0}(A_b)_{pp}|V_p(z)|^2,$$ where $a_p=U_pb_p+V_pb_p^*$ is the inverse of [en:bogoliubov], with the phase of $z$ restored. Then $0\le T_A(z)\le Cv_b$ and $$\begin{aligned} \left|\langle\xi,\mathrm d\Gamma(A_b)\xi\rangle -T_A(z)\|\xi\|^2\right| &\le C(1+R^2)\mathcal Q_z(\xi)\nonumber\\ &\quad+C\{(1+R^2)\mathcal Q_z(\xi) T_A(z)\|\xi\|^2\}^{1/2}. \label{en:observable-bound} \end{aligned}$$ The constant is independent of $A_b$.

The constants in Definition 18 can be chosen so that $$\label{lp:good-probability-bounds} \mathbb P\{v\text{ is bad}\}\leq C(x)D^{-1-1/8}, \qquad \mathbb P\{A\text{ consists of bad sites}\}\leq p^{|A|}$$ for every site $v$ and every set $A$ of distinct sites. Here $p>0$ can be any prescribed fixed constant, followed by a sufficiently large lower threshold on $D$. Failure of the full-path event in a fixed neighborhood has probability at most $C(x)D^{-6}$. The estimates are uniform in $\Phi$ and in all sufficiently large torus sizes $K$.

Fix the exposed data in a good neighborhood. Let $k$ be a deterministic path satisfying its individual cutoffs, and let $i\ne k$ have the eligible endpoints. Under $B_i$, the probability that the trial satisfies its own cutoffs and comes within distance $r$ of path $k$ is at most $\beta_{ik}$. For two legs pinned at a prescribed midpoint $y$, with $|y-m_i|\leq8b$ and $d_K(y,\omega_k(0))>s$, the bound has the additional term $$\frac{b_D}{s\vee d_K(y,\omega_k(0))}.$$ If $y$ is instead uniform in a unit cell at a fixed bounded distance from $m_i$, the integrated collision probability, including failure of this midpoint separation, is at most $C\beta_{ik}$.

Fix good data in all neighborhoods met by the following trials. In the first three assertions existing unexposed paths may take any values satisfying their individual cutoffs, while the frozen paths remain those of the fixed data. The fourth assertion instead concerns an obstacle collection satisfying the full-path bounds. For all sufficiently large $D$, these assertions hold also when an arbitrary subset of avoidance checks is omitted.*

1.  *An ordinary trial $B_i$, required to satisfy its own cutoffs and avoid the frozen paths and all indicated other unexposed paths, succeeds with probability at least $3/4$.*

2.  *A trial formed by choosing a uniform midpoint in a unit cell contained in $B(m_i,8b)$ and at an absolute constant distance from its mean, then choosing independent bridge legs, has success probability at least $3/4$. It may also be required to have midpoint distance greater than $s$ from every opponent.*

3.  *Two such trials in two copies, using a common unit cell meeting the preceding conditions for both labels, with a common uniform midpoint and independent legs conditional on that midpoint, simultaneously succeed with probability at least $1/2$. Each is checked against the previously present paths in its own copy; the pair is not checked against itself across the copies.*

4.  *Suppose the entire obstacle collection satisfies the motion and count bounds defining the full-path event. A trial pinned at any point within $8b$ of its mean and more than $s$ from every obstacle midpoint succeeds with probability at least $3/4$. This remains valid after adding or substituting a fixed number of individually allowed obstacles, provided the indicated endpoint and midpoint separations hold.

Fix good data and a set of route labels $S\subset\mathcal I$ with a bounded number of labels per site. In a product of their free bridge probabilities, condition on individual cutoffs and any selection of avoidance checks, including checks against fixed outside paths. The paths with labels in $\mathcal I\setminus S$ need only satisfy their individual cutoffs; the frozen paths remain those of the fixed good data. Every specified $q$ labels have joint marginal density at most $C^q$ relative to the product of their $B_i$. The conclusion also holds conditional on the values of all other labels. A uniform-midpoint insertion has the additional density expense $CD^{Cx}$ for each inserted marginal, or in an augmented integral retaining the common midpoint, and replacing one free midpoint density by that of a neighboring label has expense [lp:midpoint-ratio].
The projection of $P_{\mathrm{aug},v}$ just described is $P_v$. The mass of $P_v$ equals $\mathbb ET_v^{\mathrm{rel}}$. Its average over either partition is one.

For every indicated cell $v$, the mass in $P_{\mathrm{aug},v}$ of tags outside $\mathcal I$ is at most $C_{x,j}D^{-1-1/8}$, uniformly in $v$. The mass lost by a failure of the required good neighborhood is at most $C_{x,j}D^{-1-1/8+x}$ for a $d$-cell and at most $C_xR^3D^{-1-1/8+x}$ for an $R$-cell. Multiplying an omission by a fixed product of relative counts costs at most a further factor $C_jD^{qx}$, with $q$ the number of factors. The same convention applies to a fixed power of the omitted relative count itself.

For adjacent $d$-cells on the retained data event one can choose [palm:label-list] of length $m\le C_x$, with $C_x=O(x^{-1/2})$, and construct two path copies with these properties:* 1. *All unselected paths are the same as in the original sample. The left path of $i$ and the right path of $j$ are also unchanged.* 2. *Both copies satisfy every path constraint defining the conditional law at the given datum.* 3. *For $1\le k\le m$, the left midpoint of $i_k$ equals the right midpoint of $i_{k-1}$. Thus, after deleting $i$ on the left and $j$ on the right, the midpoint configurations agree as unordered lists.* 4. *The construction is a probability kernel conditional on the original sample and the route choices.* *Consequently, weighting by [palm:two-tag-weight], averaging all choices, and ordering the common remaining midpoint list uniformly defines a single finite measure $\nu_{v,w}$ on the remaining particles.

Write $\beta_{lk}$ for the collision bound in Lemma 20, and set $$\beta_* = C_xD^{-19/100}.$$ Suppose either that the four changed sets are disjoint, or that they have exactly one independent label identification. After increasing $D$ the following bounds hold for their centered likelihoods, integrated against the conditional reference on their union. Finite differences act on the entire admissibility numerator and its likelihood factors; the original conditional-reference normalizer is held fixed.* 1. *A finite difference that switches one block-pair interaction has absolute integral at most $C_xD^{C\sqrt x}$ times the sum of the $\beta_{lk}$ for the finitely many label pairs checked across that interaction. In particular it is at most $C_xD^{C\sqrt x}\beta_*$.* 2. *If all four lists have disjoint changed sets, a mixed difference in two distinct block-pair interactions has absolute integral at most $C_xD^{C\sqrt x}$ times a finite sum of products $\beta_{lk}\beta_{l'k'}$, with one checked pair from each interaction.* *The bounds are valid if additional switches have already been fixed on or off. The number of summands is bounded by a constant depending only on $x$.

At fixed retained data and route sites, the label average of the error in [long:disjoint-product], together with the contribution of all choices having $S\cap T\ne\varnothing$, is at most $$\label{long:label-error} C D^{-1+\zeta(x)}J_*e^{\delta_D J}, \qquad \delta_D\longrightarrow0, \qquad \zeta(x)\longrightarrow0\quad(x\downarrow0).$$ This estimate includes the normalized sums over the three tag labels at their specified mean-sites. The remaining weight of each tag site is at most $CR^{-3}$.

Put $Q_R=P_R-P_0$. Uniformly over normalized, possibly complex, bosonic ground vectors, $$\label{asm:infrared-bound}
 D\|(Q_R)_1\Phi\|_2^2\le16\epsilon_j+o(1)+o_K(1),$$ where $\epsilon_j\to0$. The coefficient $16$ is independent of $j$; the dilute remainder may depend on $j$. The exponents $u,w$ and the scale $R$ may be kept fixed when $j$ is increased; all dilute and volume thresholds may depend on $j$.

For every fixed $H<\infty$, $$\label{mom:characteristic-limit} \int e^{ih\cdot p}\,\mathrm d\mathfrak m_\Phi(p) =\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{ih\cdot p}F_\alpha(p) \frac{\mathrm dp}{(2\pi)^3}+o(1), \qquad |h|\le H.$$ The error is uniform in $h$ and in normalized, possibly complex, ground vectors, with the iterated-limit convention of Section 2.
